name: Marble Museum
basis: why: relief with only a few centimetres of depth, form by slopes catching light; how: brightness as stone height lit by one spotlight

lumenary.blurb: A relief in a gallery: the picture carved shallow into veined marble, polished, hung on a dark wall under one spotlight, with a brass plate beneath it.

facts.bestOn: Portraits and figures lit from one side

why: A relief is sculpture that stays attached to its wall. The carver has only a few centimetres of depth, so form is suggested by slopes that catch the light. Marble adds its own character: it lets light sink in a little, which softens every shadow, and it is crossed by veins that ignore the carving completely. One spotlight in a dark room does the rest.
how: Use the picture’s brightness, mostly blurred, as the height of the stone.
Find the slope at each pixel and light it from the spotlight’s direction.
Darken the hollows and add a polished highlight.
Colour the stone with soft clouding, and draw veins where a warped noise crosses its middle.
Hang the slab on a dark wall with a shadow, lit edges and a brass plate.
history: Relief is among the oldest forms of sculpture, from Egyptian tomb walls to the marble frieze of the Parthenon, carved around 440 BC. In fifteenth-century Florence Donatello developed rilievo schiacciato, “flattened relief”, in which a scene is modelled in a depth of millimetres. White marble from Carrara in Tuscany has been quarried since Roman times and was the stone of Michelangelo.
uses: Book covers for history and classics
terms: Low relief: carving that projects only slightly from its background.
A streak of other minerals running through marble.
Light entering a material, bouncing about inside and leaving nearby.
paragraphs: A relief keeps the big forms of its subject and only hints at the small ones. The height map is therefore mostly a well-blurred copy of the brightness with a share of the sharp picture mixed in, set by the “fine chisel work” slider. Slopes of that map give a normal at every pixel. Marble lets light a little way in before scattering it back, so the diffuse term is gentle and clamped well above black. Hollows collect shade: where the surface lies below its own local average it is darkened by up to half. Polish adds a tight highlight and a faint broad one.

The stone itself is three layers of noise. Soft clouding blends the two body colours. Veins appear where a warped fractal noise crosses its middle value: folding the noise about one half turns that crossing into a ridge, and a high power thins the ridge to a line. A second, finer set is added the same way. On the gallery wall the slab is drawn at four fifths of the width with a shadow thrown away from the spotlight, its cut edges are lit or dimmed according to the side the light comes from, and a brass plate carries the title.

equations.note: Height: broad forms plus a share q of fine detail (the chisel slider, 0 to 1).
Shading: soft diffuse light times the darkening of hollows; h̄ is the local average height.
N₁ and N₂ are warped fractal noises at two scales; the fold makes a ridge where each crosses one half.

presets.text: Deep carving with fine chisel work brings out a face.
Black Marquina with high polish is the most dramatic stone.
Take it off the wall to use the stone as a texture.
